title: Quinn White
text:
PhD Student in Biostatistics
University of Washington
I’m currently a fourth-year PhD student at the University of Washington.
Email






Broadly, I’m interested in how we can develop methods that support clinical decision-making. From a methods standpoint, I’m interested in the ways we communicate uncertainty around what we estimate to be the recommended decisions. Accordingly, my dissertation work under Marco Carone and Andrea Rotnitzky focuses on notions of uncertainty for individualized treatment rules. My interests fall into the realms of non- and semiparametric theory and causal inference.
My applied work under Robyn McClelland has primarily focused on the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA), where I collaborate with clinicians to investigate associations between cardiovascular biomarkers and time-to-event clinical outcomes. My work on the MESA Risk Score further deepened my interest in the development, evaluation, and communication of tools like risk scores for informing clinical decisions.


Outside of research, you’ll generally find me out on my bike or with my two lovely dogs.

title: Quinn White
text:
Principal Investigator | 2024–2025 
The American Heart Association’s Debiasing Clinical Care Algorithms program supports trainees in conducting independent research examining the use of race and ethnicity in clinical decision-making algorithms. As the PI of this award, I led our project, titled “Re-evaluating the Role of Race/Ethnicity in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (MESA) Coronary Heart Disease Risk Score,” under the guidance of Robyn McClelland.
Our work focused on developing and evaluating a race-free version of the MESA Risk Score, with the goal of understanding how removing race and ethnicity as predictors affects cardiovascular risk prediction.
